facts: The token consumer forwards its JSON value to its caller-supplied success callable.

The 64-byte authentication-transaction success callable forwards the same JSON reference: its x2 argument remains untouched through the normal virtual callback call. Missing pseudoC parameters alone do not prove an argument is ignored.
The model sign-in success callable emits the native sign-in success event without reading JSON fields.
The concrete model sign-in setup passes that event callable into signInWithCallback.
The callback variant creates an authentication transaction and installs a typed authentication-request factory before running it.
The typed request factory invokes the current 236-byte sign-in request builder, passing native provider-derived arguments and the saved nonce object; provider bodies and values were not inspected.

Transaction run queues an optional pre-auth command, nonce retrieval, an intermediate authentication command and the final auth request. The pre-auth command is current PingAPI; its supported skip_device_token flag disables the following GenerateToken platform-token branch. Exact source pins and scope are in bootstrap-ping-contract.json.
The callback success forwarder retains response/JSON arguments for queued delivery. No complete startup success is claimed from that forwarding alone.
pending: Integrate internally constructed ping/nonce/sign-in handlers with trusted native owner/scope and approved origins before install, retaining closed unsupported-request behavior.
Verify queued success delivery, owner invalidation and complete offline login inside the original client.
scope_limits: The 64-byte success decompilation follows five sites into one separate 60-byte body; only the within-64-byte normal-success path supplies the stated unchanged-x2 forwarding fact.
The eight-byte dispatch callable tails into a separate 172-byte body; this is observed separately, not described as an eight-byte implementation.
Each of the three setup-container decompilations remains within its own declared body.
No secrets, source/account keys, private values, raw instructions, decompiled code or addresses are published.
